## TL;DR

I ran a headless WebKit QA pass on the Checks page live run view at 375, 768 and 1280 px, using seeded fixtures for four states: running, queued, stalled and failed. Two real problems turned up and are fixed. A running check's heading overflowed its box at phone and tablet widths when the machine name had no break point, and a failed "Release slot" was silent on the Now tab. A successful release also said nothing about what it did. All three are fixed and covered by a new WebKit test that passes (9 tests). The QA doc is at `docs/qa/2026-11-checks-live-run-qa.md`.

One gap I did not fix: the Checks page has no cancel or retry control for a live check run. Those controls live on the task card and in the close-out status bar, so this pass could not test them on this page.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for the live run view and its cancel and retry controls to be checked for four run states at three widths, with output staying inside its box. Before writing any test I read the Now tab, the Test suite panel and the close-out pipeline summary, and I searched the UI for cancel and retry wording. On the Checks page, the only action on a live run is "Release slot" for a wedged local slot. It opens a confirmation dialog. "Cancel stalled check" is on `TaskCard.vue`, and close-out cancel and retry are in `IntegrationStatusBar.vue`. I did not add cancel or retry buttons to the Checks page. That would be a product change, and the task asked for QA plus fixes.

I built the harness on the pattern in `checks-releases-data-responsive.test.ts`. It runs a Vite server with a per-test alias that swaps `../stores/repo` for a seeded stub, mocks every `/api/**` call through Playwright routing, and mounts the real `ChecksView`. The state seeds live in `tests/fixtures/checks-live-run-states.ts`, and the mocked API responses come from the same seed, so the two cannot drift. I deliberately used an unbroken 140-character machine name and a 120-character error path with no spaces, because those are the cases a box with no wrap rule fails on.

Two fixes followed from the failures:

- The running check's heading row had no wrap and the grid had no `min-width: 0`. With the unbroken machine name, the box passed the viewport at 375 and 768 px, and the progress line escaped its section. I made the heading wrap, gave the machine name `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, and set the section grid to `minmax(0, 1fr)`.
- The release error was set on the page-level `error` ref, which only renders on the Check plan tab. On the Now tab a failed release closed the dialog and showed nothing. I added `slotActionError`, shown as an alert in the Local check slots section, and the dialog now closes on failure so the message is not hidden behind it.

The success path also had no feedback, so I added `slotActionNotice`. It reads "Released slot N (PID P). The check process group it held was stopped." The dialog copy already says that process group is terminated, so the notice reports what the dialog promised.

## Approaches tried

My first harness attempt failed for three harness-only reasons, none of them app bugs. The store stub did not export `COLUMNS` and `sortTasks`, which the Checks tree imports at link time, so I copied those from the existing stub. Pages with several states timed out at vitest's 5 s default, so I gave those tests 60 s. Most importantly, the fixture's router push rewrote the URL and dropped `liveState`, so every page rendered the default running seed and the failed assertion saw queued text. I now keep `liveState` in the pushed route.

The layout assertions passed on the first real run with a hyphenated machine name. Hyphens are legal break points, so the test proved very little. Only the unbroken name exposed the overflow. I kept the unbroken name in the fixture because a test that cannot fail is not a QA check.

I also considered a visual screenshot pass. I did not take one. The assertions measure each box against the viewport and its container, which is more reliable than a picture for this class of bug.

## Challenges and blockers

The main limit is that cancel and retry are not on the Checks page. I stated that in the QA doc rather than building controls there, so a human should decide whether they belong on this page.

Everything here is synthetic. The states come from fixture data, not from a live RepoOS server, so this does not show what a real stalled check looks like on a real machine. I did not start a real check run, as the task required.

The first `repoos check` run failed on formatting in my three changed files, which I fixed with `bunx oxfmt`. The second run passed: format, lint, build, CSS layers, theme contrast, hardcoded colors, bare-require, branch artifacts, UI smoke and the remote validation test run (passed in 234 s on the runner).

## Key learnings

A layout test is only as good as its worst input. A hyphenated fixture passed at every width, and an unbroken one failed at two. Pick inputs that have no break points for any box that renders user-controlled text, such as hostnames, paths and error output.

A failure path needs to show somewhere the user is looking. Here, the error existed and was set correctly, but it rendered on a different tab. A test that asserts the alert is visible on the Now tab catches that, and a test that only asserts the API was called does not.

Actions that change state should say what they did. The dialog promised a process would be stopped, and the page then said nothing. A short confirmation that names the slot and PID closes that gap at almost no cost.
